title: Functional connectomics reveals general wiring rule in mouse visual cortex
goal: Reproduce the original biological like-to-like wiring and common-input-versus-functional-similarity findings from the source neuron and edge measurements, preserving anatomical/projection controls, measured versus model-derived features, and the original GLMM/bootstrap comparisons within the single reconstructed mouse volume. Assess improvement of the same biological result only under a separately justified criterion. Retain Figure 6 RNN classification and ablation findings as a separately named modeling result, not a substitute for biological reproduction or improvement.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: Biological like-to-like wiring and common-input-versus-functional-similarity relationships from the single reconstructed mouse volume, retaining source anatomical/projection controls and GLMM/bootstrap comparisons; not an every-figure or whole-paper requirement.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: artificial_network_modeling: Figure 6 RNN image classification, connection ablations, like-to-like relationships and common-input analogues remain genuine separately named modeling results; artificial units/images/runs do not replace biological neurons/edges or their inference.
empirical_model_validation: Digital-twin fidelity and measured-versus-model-derived response validation remain distinct source evidence, relevant to feature interpretation but not a replacement primary performance score; no digital-twin retraining is added.
prospective_extension: New anatomical-subdivision, distance/type/opportunity-preserving null or edge-prediction designs remain extensions, not recovered original numerical superiority targets.
success_criteria: Recreate the corrected primary empirical findings with their source-defined populations, complete required panels and controls.
Use an explicitly bound reproduction proposal only within its declared eligibility, comparison and execution limits; copying published findings is insufficient.

The preserved improvement.v1.json retains its declared comparison and coverage. Use retained_secondary_scope for its relationship to the corrected primary findings; satisfying a secondary or partial-component criterion alone does not establish complete primary reproduction or improvement.

The primary same-target outcome bundle is unavailable. Any primary improvement requires an independently justified source-grounded comparison; no replacement metric, direction or tolerance is invented.
Keep the paper+data and paper+data+author-code outcomes separate. All scientific outcomes remain unknown until qualifying original-data execution and independent verification.
Preserve prior task definitions, improvement criteria and useful secondary implementations with their original scopes. Historical attempts and source metadata do not become qualified AI results.
